fatigue.detail: Plain rolled bottom flange; welded attachments are checked separately in the detail register.

notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier, site and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 5 simply supported 30-ft bays, W33X354 girders, two 40-ton cab cranes, on new freestanding W14X730 columns with welded haunched rib seats, base plates, anchor rods and spread footings, and crane-level rod X-bracing; the existing building carries no crane load. Seismic: ordinary steel cantilever column system across the runway and rod bracing not specifically detailed for seismic resistance along it, Seismic Design Category B. A direct flange saddle does not suit this rolled girder (the sized saddle leaves saddle-across-fatigue 3.51, flange-tie-saddle-fatigue 1.65 for the estimated tie demands; a welded saddle is a Category D/E attachment on the top flange of this high-cycle runway (CMAA Class D, AIST Class B)): the paired flat bars bolt to the tie-side bearing stiffener, cut as one plate with its gusset extension past the flange tip (no weld at the gusset), the full-depth stiffener pair carrying the tie force into the girder. Fixed at both ends at this reach, the paired bars cannot follow the girder end rotation and thermal travel along the runway (the tie movement checks over their limits): the column gusset slides 14 mm each way along the runway on longer sleeves (column-end slide, fillers at the girder gusset; checks tie-slide-*). Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier. The bracket stays: the W10X112 crane-level strut is moment-connected in plan at every column by 13 mm plates on its flanges (torsion brace, 4 rows of bolt pairs) and holds the new W14X730 columns against the twist: 0.0109 rad factored (limit 0.02) and 3 mm of bearing movement at every crane start and stop (limit 26 mm). The girder's twist movement under the factored traction is 5 mm, above the 2 mm (a configurator target, tightened from 1/8 in where the tie could not take the movement, not a code limit): the W10X112 is the stiffest strut that fits the torsion plates, and the tie, slots and gaps take this movement in their checks. With the strut on the column centerline alone, the girder seated 792 mm off the column axis, the traction twists the column 0.0278 rad factored (limit 0.02) and 7 mm of bearing movement at every crane start and stop (limit 26 mm).

selections.reason: The support reaction, about 975 kN (220 kip), is above the AIST TR-13 §5.9.2 guideline of 222 kN (50 kip) for column brackets, a clause to be verified: consider column caps over the new columns; an advisory, not a code limit, so the support entered (Haunched (tapered) rib seat) is kept and checked here.

selections.designed: Paired flat bars on a bearing-stiffener gusset
selections.reason: A direct flange saddle does not suit this rolled girder (the sized saddle leaves saddle-across-fatigue 3.51, flange-tie-saddle-fatigue 1.65 for the estimated tie demands; a welded saddle is a Category D/E attachment on the top flange of this high-cycle runway (CMAA Class D, AIST Class B)): the paired flat bars bolt to the tie-side bearing stiffener, cut as one plate with its gusset extension past the flange tip (no weld at the gusset), the full-depth stiffener pair carrying the tie force into the girder. Fixed at both ends at this reach, the paired bars cannot follow the girder end rotation and thermal travel along the runway (the tie movement checks over their limits): …

Lightest compact W within the sizing targets (ratio ≤ 0.85, deflections ≤ 0.9 of the limits): screening estimates, top-flange tip stress (DG7, warping and second-order twist) ratio 0.77, vertical deflection 0.37, lateral 0.56 and rail-head movement with twist 0.77 of their limits; flanges at least 286 mm wide for the end bearing bolt gauge and the rail seat; lighter candidates rejected: 90 by sizing ratio, 75 by flange width; the next lighter, W36X350: tips ratio 1.05 > 0.85; lateral deflection 1.04 of the limit > 0.9; rail-head movement with twist 1.30 of the limit > 0.9. These are the configurator's screening estimates (a simplified model that ranks the catalog), not the final ratios: the calculation checks the section and reports its own ratios.

New cantilever column for a 40-ton crane (W14X120 to 5 t, W14X159 to 12.5 t, W14X211 to 25 t, else W14X257). The W14X257 chosen for the crane gives base drift ratio 7.39 > 0.9 and column torsion ratio 1.45 > 1.00: no W14 to the W14X730 meets the new column's drift, torsion and twist ratios for this crane; the heaviest searched, W14X730, lowers the governing ratio and is built, still giving base drift ratio 2.12: an open item (New column beyond the W14 range).

selections.designed: Haunched (tapered) rib seat, at its sizing limits, kept
selections.reason: The Haunched (tapered) rib seat sized to the limits of its steps still exceeds fatigue-rib 1.82, fatigue-rootWeld 1.61, fatigue-seat 1.54, fatigue-seatWeld 1.37 (sizing estimates; the calculation reports its own) for the 976.789 kN support reaction (configurator estimate, with the support steel), about 4.4 times the AIST TR-13 §5.9.2 guideline of 222.411 kN (a clause to be verified; the calculation's column-bracket check reports its own reaction and ratio): a bracket is beyond reasonable use for this crane on a freestanding cantilever column. Recommended: column caps over the new columns (support column-cap), the girder bearing on the column axis; the support entered is kept and checked (review draft).

Weld-on clip bases on the top flange are an AISC Table A-3.1 item 7.1 attachment, Category D: the estimated top-plate range 132.4 MPa (rated-lift crane moment without impact plus the top-flange lateral bending under the side thrust) at all 500,000 cycles exceeds F_SR = 113.0 MPa (ratio 1.17, the project's all-cycle method). Bolted clamp plates leave holes for pretensioned bolts (item 2.2, Category B), as AISC DG7 and AIST TR-13 allow.

selections.designed: paired-bars, closest; tie to be designed by hand
selections.reason: Top-flange tie not resolved: the Paired flat bars on the bearing stiffener, as sized for the estimated tie demands, still exceeds tie-move-root-fatigue 2.44, tie-move-gusset 1.30, tie-move-fatigue 1.02 (configurator estimates), and no other tie arrangement the configurator tries fits and passes here. Recommended: column caps over the new columns (support column-cap): the girder bears on the column axis, so the traction no longer twists the column at a bracket seat, and the end fork on the cap (the girder's bearing stiffeners with the couple of its bearing bolts) replaces the top-flange tie; the configurator does not build that alternative here. Otherwise design the tie connection by hand.

selections.designed: W14X730, closest; new column beyond the W14 range
selections.reason: New column beyond the W14 range: the heaviest W14 searched, W14X730, still gives base drift ratio 2.12 (configurator estimate; the calculation reports its own). Column caps on the W14X730 would leave about 0.67 of the drift limit for the column alone, 0.84 with this footing's rotation (estimate without the eccentric reaction moment and seat twist). Recommended: column caps over the new columns (support column-cap: the girder on the column axis, no eccentric reaction moment, no seat twist). The support entered is kept and checked.

fabrication.steel: Girder ASTM A992; plates, bars and stiffeners ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves. Rail joints thermite or flash-butt welded by the rail supplier's qualified procedure (preheat, grinding, inspection); no joint bars or bolts.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
